To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the livers of rats that had been fed the carcinogen 3′- Me-DAB had a lower nucleic acid content than the livers of control rats.
the nucleic acid and enzyme contents of the livers and mitochondrial fractions of rats fed 3-Me-DAB were significantly lower than those of rats fed 4-DAB.

the livers of rats given the noncarcinogen, 2-Methyl-4-diaminoazobenzne, or the carcinogenic dye, 3′Methyl-4-dianinoazobenzine, were characterized by an increased nucleic acid content, and by an increased activity of all enzymes studied except octanoxidase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the enzymatic and chemical studies of the livers and their mitochondria of rats which have been fed 2-Me or 3-Me-DAB for 4 weeks.
the effects of 3-Me-DAB on the enzymic activity and nucleic acid content of the livers and the mitochondria of the livers of rats.
the enzymatic and chemical changes which occur in the livers and the mitochondrial fractions of livers from rats fed 2-Me- or 3′- Me-DAB.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the livers of rats receiving the carcinogenic dye, 3′ -Me-DAB, contained significantly less RNA than those of rats receiving the noncarcinogen, 2-MelAB.

the livers and mitochondria of the rats fed either the basal diet or the basal diet supplemented with the carcinogenic azo dye 3′- Me-DAB showed significant increases in their nucleic acid contents and their enzymatic activities.
the livers of rats given a commercial chow or a semi-synthesized basal diet were not different in their nucleic acid and enzymatic content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the livers and the mitochondrial fractions of rats fed the carcinogenic azo dye 3′-M-DAB, or of those fed the noncarcinogen 2-MeDAB, showed little change in their nucleic acids and their enzymatic activities, except for the succinoxidase activity of the liver mitochondria.
the livers of rats given 3′-methyl-DAB showed no significant differences in nucleic acid content, or enzymatic activities when compared to the livers of the control groups.

2-Me- or 3′- Me-DAB feeding did not significantly alter the liver nucleic acid content, nor did the carcinogen feeding significantly alter the enzymatic activity of either the liver or the liver mitochondria, except that the uricase activity of both the liver and mitochondria of rats on the carcinogen-supplemented diets was slightly higher than that of the controls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3′- Me-DAB feeding results in a marked decrease in liver weight, RNA, and RNA polymerase activity.

the livers of rats given 3-Me-DAB were characterized by a significant decrease in their nucleic acid and enzymatic content, while the liver mitochondria showed a marked decrease in their nucleotides and succinoxidase activity.
3-Me-DAB is a potent hepatocarcinogen in the rat and is capable of inducing a wide range of enzymatic changes in the liver and in the liver mitochondria.
